title: 'One Size Does Not Fit All': A Roadmap of Purpose-Driven Mixed-Method Pathways for Sensitivity Analysis of Agent-Based Models
publisher: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (JASSS)

key_points.claim: Sensitivity analysis (SA) method choice for ABMs should depend on the model's purpose; no single method fits all.
key_points.evidence_quote: no single SA method fits all ABMs and that different methods of SA should be used based on the overarching purpose of the model

key_points.claim: Abstract exploratory models need only simple SA, as they use limited data on patterns or stylized facts.
key_points.evidence_quote: For them, simple SA methods may be sufficient in capturing the dependencies between the output-input spaces.

key_points.claim: Applied, data-rich policy/scenario models need more sophisticated SA to establish robustness before results reach end-users.
key_points.evidence_quote: the choice of a more sophisticated SA may be critical in establishing the robustness of the results

key_points.claim: Paper offers a roadmap for choosing SA and advocates routine use of global methods that capture input interactions.
key_points.evidence_quote: advocates for the routine use of global methods that capture input interactions

key_points.claim: Frontier SA methods: spatial/temporal outputs, whole output distributions, topological relationships, and finding behavioral primitives to study regime shifts and tipping points.
key_points.evidence_quote: finding behavioral primitives and using them to study complex system characteristics like regime shifts, tipping points, and condensation versus dissipation of collective system behavior

reliability_notes: Peer-reviewed JASSS review paper. The fetch returned the full text, but I only read the abstract and metadata before running out of tool calls, so all points come from the abstract. It covers methodology (SA/validation) rather than the content of artificial societies.
